"Don't Snuff the Prof"

"The average man's fate is no longer in his own hands...but in those of
politicians, corporations, executives and remote, anonymous
technicians." (128)

"Man in the future will be no longer a creation of Nature... but a
manufactured
product." (122)

"The technophiles are taking us all on an utterly reckless ride into the
unknown."(180) 


                        "There's a little bit of 
                              The
                       Unabomber
                            in all of us."
                        - Robert Wright, TIME Magazine



The Unabomber killed people, and that was wrong. I am very sorry that
innocent
people were hurt and killed. Nevertheless, there is widespread sympathy
for the
ideas expressed in his Manifesto and for the suspect, Dr. Theodore
Kaczynski, as a
person. Many people, including myself, view progress and technology as a
threat
and have admitted to a certain respect for the Unabomber for saying so,
even if
they do not agree with his violent tactics. The Federal Justice system
has already
determined they will seek the death penalty for Dr. Kaczynski if he is
convicted.
Many people, including myself, do not wish to see this happen. This page
is a
collection of quotes from such people, collected as a protest against
such a
possibility. Let us tell the authorities: Please don't "snuff" the Prof!

Sources: Unless otherwise stated, these comments came from a year's
worth of
posts on the alt.fan.unabomber newsgroup. All names have been omitted.
Some
messages have been edited for clarity.

Who we are:

These quotes are from people all over the US, as well as Canada, England
and
Germany. We are: college students in biology and history, anthropology
professors,
computer programmers and systems analysts, moms with children, desktop
publishers and working stiffs of various kinds. Many, of course, have
not wished to
divulge personal information about themselves.



"I'm very pleased that someone intelligent is addressing the problems of
our
society...the Unabomber was brave enough to discuss the current state of
humanity
when no one else could. He had the vision to see the error in blind
pursuit of
technology..."

"People call him a killer, but he was defending our planet. People will
kill to defend their country, what about the planet?"

"If the Unabomber was just a killer not many people would be a fan of
him. It is his brilliant interpretations of our society that we're fans
of."

"He dared to say what most people are too afraid, oversocialized, or
blind to say. He confronted our social problems with a thoughtful
analysis which is rare in a time when media stupidity is the main source
of most people's "information" about the world around them."

"He is ... a symbol that the human spirit has not yet been killed... he
has started a dialog on the most forbidden subject in our society: the
meaning of our existance, behavior, values and future."

"The Unabomber may have killed people but he has many redeeming
qualities."

"The Unabomber was right: technology is a raging monster that has made
us all
feebleminded drones, and eventually it is going to kill us."

"If one condemns the violence one also has to condemn any institutional
violence, say capital punishment or killing in war. Otherwise it just
means that ethics lines  neatly with the purposes of the state...a group
of people who are in power...and it's not real ethics, just the
self-justification of power."

"Sometimes drastic social situations call for drastic actions to remedy
them."

"While WE (the techno savvy) sit on our asses & stare at our screens to
rant about the power the government and large businesses have over us,
HE's the man who's trying to change things and ENLIGHTEN people to our
own self destruction."

"Look at the world today, is it a peaceful place? Do you think it will
ever be? What do you think made the world such a shit hole to live in in
the first place? If you haven't read the manifesto yet, DO so. You will
find the answers to these questions in it."

"In truth if his tinkerings had come at a different time in history, if
his thinking had gained more adherents, if his one man "movement" had
gained momentum, he might have been called a visionary, or at least a
revolutionary."

"Based on the Manifesto, I think he's in vastly better shape than
99.999% of
humanity."

"FC's greatest fear was genetic engineering and other technologies that
will control our minds and irreversibly enslave us. This... is so
frightening and inevitable to him that he regards any means as aceptable
to fight against it."

"I don't agree with his killings, but I do agree with his points. He is
not a serial killer, he is a revolutionary."

"The unabomber is a man who stands in the face of the evil powers that
will
eventually lead to the downfall of society."

"Almost all countries have achieved their independence by terrorism.
Whoever
wrote the manifesto was deeply concerned with the future freedom of
humanity..."

"[the unabomber] kills for a noble cause and he's a "murderer",
capitalists kill millions and obliterate Nature, and it's called
"business".

"When humans do screw up the planet... perhaps society will collapse and
the
Unabomber will have the last laugh from his grave or whatever."

"The Unabomber's Manifesto is a very honest and enlightening work. I
agree with
many of the views expressed... I think it's a shame that holders of
minority
opinions..have to resort to such drastic measures to get the attention
they deserve."

"The Unabomber, whoever he is, is "right on" about society." 

"The manifesto makes a lot of sense." 

"IMHO, the people who go around imposing themselves and their idea of
progress
on everyone else, often at a fatal cost to members of their own species,
other
species and the environment in general are more psychopathic than the
Unabomber. At least the Unabomber thought out his actions morally. I see
no
indications that the progress crowd even thinks about what they do."

Supporters' Descriptions of Selves

"I work in a research lab in biology at Yale, and hence I and most of my
social
circle are potentially on the hit list. We, too, are fascinated by the
Unabomber, and sympathtic to much of his message. "

"I'd like to throw my minor in comparative history, ideas and culture
behind me
when I say TK has made an important intellectual contribution to our
society. "

"An interviewer with the Sacramento Bee said that 'a lot of the sympathy
expressed for the Unabomber was from computer people...the very people
he was against.' "

"My father...has been a business executive since college...he agreed
with [una's] basic conclusions and told me of some of his business
acquaintances who agreed with a lot of [Una's beliefs]."

"I have a job and a girlfriend, two dogs and my own home, and still
admire the
Unabomber." [from an article in a British zine, name not available at
present.]

"Computer users are often intelligent and creative and these are the
people who
realize the direction in which our society is going. Some of them, such
as myself, may identify with Kaczynski because, like him, they may have
suffered rejection and loneliness because they were 'nerds' or different
from the norm."

Personal Sympathy for Theodore Kaczynski

"I think Kaczynski is an interesting character, and one whom people are
sadly
mislabling and misjudging." 

"TK/FC/Unabomb is inspiring to me simply because he/she/they/it is one
of those
very rare people with a passion for something other than money."

"I ...sympathize with TK. This is a man with a special gift that he was
unable to use, because of a disability that he could not find a way to
overcome... TK's life, in one sense, is a tragedy and a cry for help. In
another sense, it is a blow struck against inhumanity, ...the
destruction of nature and people by technology and corporate and
government greed." 

"I think Kaczynski is a deep thinker...and he may turn out to have been
quite
right." 

"TK is a sort of hero to me ... he's a fascinating character...an
accomplished person who thumbs his nose at bourgeous culture and does
things that... go beyond plain old love of self... it's epic stuff to
me."

"I felt that despite his [alleged] crimes, he had a lot of potential for
growth and change."

"He...strikes me as a vulnerable person who protected himself with
isolation...and he also seems fundamentally good, fundamentally
idealistic, and someone of much personal power."

"Ted is a misunderstood boy genius, with more intellect than that of the
[whole] US government combined. His ideas for the ceasing of technology
prove he was a great man, who took the wrong way about handling things."

"Ted K. is visibly not a monster. He's a brilliant, sensitive man who
let us know what he felt and did what he did for reasons that many of us
relate to. Many of us might even feel that in the ultimate...maybe,
history will prove him right." 

The Death Penalty

"It would be particularly horrible to see [TK executed]. He is alienated
from society for reasons that many of us can relate to: the wholesale
destruction of nature and runaway technology whose development is driven
by dollars, not by humanity's long-term best interest. He was apparently
conducting a one-man war against evils that many of us oppose. If he
were part of an army, he would be considered a prisoner of war and
executing him would be a war crime. 
Ted Kaczynski has a lot to offer the world. His (?) manifesto was
brilliant and
thought provoking. If you killed him off, you would be killing a radical
and
perceptive social critic."

"I will die a little more if he is executed. Maybe our society and all
the people will die a little more."

"You should [not] have to look hard to find many parallels of people
with multiple motives for killing, from discussions of the death penalty
to ditties sung celebrating enemy deaths in war."

"There presently is widespread sentiment against imposition of the death
penalty in this case. ( in the NY Times forum, sentiment was running
10-0 against it.)...some of the Unabomber's victims see no reason to
kill Kaczynski if he's convicted."
